NEERAJ P. DHOTE, J.
 DATED : 06.03.2026.
ORAL JUDGMENT

This is an Appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short "M.V. Act") by the Claimant against the judgment and order dated 10.12.2013, passed by the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Nagpur in Claim Petition No.902/2005 dismissing the Claim Petition which was filed under Section 166 of the M.V. Act.
2 fa938.2015.odt 2.
Heard the learned Advocate for the Appellant and learned Advocate for the Insurance Company.
With their assistance perused the papers on record.

3. It is submitted by the learned Advocate for the Appellant that, it was the case of composite negligence as the Appellant was travelling as a Passenger in the Jeep insured with the Respondent Ramesh S/O Ganpatrao Rajas vs Aslam Ayyub Qureshi And Anothers on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115120312/

sentences.text: He submitted that, the Claimant examined himself to show that, the Driver of the said Jeep i.e. Respondent No.1, was also responsible for the accident.
He submitted that, the Tribunal did not consider the evidence on record in its right perspective.

In support of his submissions, he relied on the judgment in Pawan Kumar and another V/s. Harkishan Dass Mohan Lal and others, (2014) 3 SCC 590 on the point of distinction between the principles of composite and contributory negligence.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He submits that, the Appeal be allowed and the compensation be awarded.
4. It is submitted by the learned Advocate for the Respondent No.2 Insurance Company that, there is no evidence on record to show that, the Respondent No.1 who was driving the Jeep was negligent.
The Appellant in his evidence accepted that, the Jeep was being driven on its proper side.
She submitted that, this is not case 3 fa938.2015.odt of composite negligence as there is no iota of evidence to show that, the Jeep Driver was at fault or negligent in driving the Jeep.
In support of her submissions, she relied on the decision dated 09.12.2025 of this Court in First Appeal No.1848/2024 (Janardhan Sitaram Surve and another V/s. Sunil Ramesh Ukrulkar and another).

sentences.text: She submitted that, the Appeal be dismissed.
5. There is no dispute on the aspect that, the above referred Claim Petition was filed by the Appellant under Section 166 of the M.V. Act.
The Jeep Driver and the Insurance Company of the Jeep were arrayed as the Respondents.
The owner, Driver and the Insurer of the Truck were not parties to the Claim Petition.

In Pawan Kumar (supra) it is observed as follows:-
"7.
The distinction between the principles of composite and contributory negligence has been dealt with in Winfield & Jolowicz on Tort (Chapter 21) (15th Edn. 1998).

It would be appropriate to notice the following passage from the said work:
"Where two or more people by their independent breaches of duty to the plaintiff cause him to suffer distinct injuries, no special rules are required, for each tortfeasor is liable for the damage which he caused and only for that damage.

Where, however,
two or more breaches of duty by different persons cause the plaintiff to suffer a single injury the position is more complicated.
The law in such a case is that the plaintiff is entitled to sue all or any of them for the full amount of his loss, and each is said to be jointly and severally liable for it.

This means that special rules are necessary to deal with the possibilities of successive actions in respect of that loss and of claims for contribution or indemnity by one tortfeasor against the others.

It is greatly to the plaintiff's advantage to show that he has suffered the same, indivisible 4 fa938.2015.odt harm at the hands of a number of defendants for he thereby avoids the risk, inherent in cases where there are different injuries, of finding that one defendant is insolvent (or uninsured) and being unable to execute judgment against him.

The same picture is not, of course, so attractive from the point of view of the solvent defendant, who may end up carrying full responsibility for a loss in the Ramesh S/O Ganpatrao Rajas vs Aslam Ayyub Qureshi And Anothers on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115120312/

sentences.text: causing of which he played only a partial, even secondary role.
The question of whether there is one injury can be a difficult one.

The simplest case is that of two virtually simultaneous acts of negligence, as where two drivers behave negligently and collide, injuring a passenger in one of the cars or a pedestrian, but there is no requirement that the acts be simultaneous..."

8. Where the plaintiff/claimant himself is found to be a party to the negligence the question of joint and several liability cannot arise and the plaintiff's claim to the extent of his own negligence, as may be quantified, will have to be severed.
In such a situation the plaintiff can only be held entitled to such part of damages/compensation that is not attributable to his own negligence.

The above principle has been explained in T.O. Anthony followed in K. Hemlatha."
6.
In the case at hand, undisputedly, the Crime was registered against the unknown Truck Driver for the accident which occurred on 21.03.2005.
The Appellant examined himself before the learned Tribunal by filing the evidence on affidavit.

The perusal of the evidence affidavit shows that, he stated on oath that, at the relevant time and place of the accident when the Mahendra Jeep was proceeding towards Parseoni an unknown vehicle came from opposite direction resulting in collision.
After giving dash, the said unknown vehicle ran away.

Though in para No.3 of the evidence 5 fa938.2015.odt affidavit it is stated that, the accident was due to rash and negligent driving on the part of the Drivers of both the vehicles, in his cross-examination the Appellant admitted that, the vehicle (in which he was travelling) was driven on the left side road.

Though in the cross-examination it has come on record that, the Jeep was being driven in the high speed, it has come on record that, the Truck came from opposite direction and dashed against their vehicle (Jeep).
This shows that, the Appellant failed to prove that, the accident was also the result of negligent driving of the Jeep by the Respondent No.1 in which he was travelling.
This being the position, the contention of learned Advocate for the Appellant that, this is the case of composite negligence has no merits.

7. The learned Tribunal in the impugned judgment observed as follows:-
"8. .....
On perusal of FIR (Exh. 29), it reveals that police have registered an offence vide Cr. No. 47/2005 against the driver of the unknown truck.
In cross-examination (PW 1) Ramesh admits that the jeep was driven on the left side of the road and the accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of the truck.
A victim of the motor accident is entitled to get the compensation u/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
If he proves that a death or permanent disability has been caused due to fault of the offending vehicle i.e. it is a fault liability.
A person, who is at fault for causing the death or permanent disability to a person by the use of motor vehicle is liable to pay compensation to him, to make him good to some extent.

Therefore, the petition is not framed properly and instituted, hence,
it is not maintainable.
Thus, I answer this issue in the negative hold that the petition is not maintainable.

sentences.text: As to Issue No.2 : On perusal of evidence of (PW 1) Ramesh, in cross-examination, he admits that the jeep in which he was traveling was driven by the left side of the road and an unknown truck which came from opposite direction dashed to the said jeep.
The said truck disappeared from the spot of incident.

From the admission given by (PW 1)
Ramesh, it is clear that the accident was not took place due to fault of the driver of respondent No.1 i.e. driver of jeep No. MH31- H-3208.

Hence, respondent no. 1 being the registered owner of the jeep in which the claimant was traveling and the respondent No.2 being the insurer of the said jeep are not liable to pay compensation as the accident was not result of the rash and negligent driving of the jeep No. MH31-H-3208.
Therefore, I answer this issue accordingly."
8. Considering the evidence available on record, no fault can be found with the observations and conclusion recorded by the learned Tribunal in dismissing the Claim Petition.
Accordingly, the Appeal is liable to be dismissed.
Hence, the following order.

ORDER i) The Appeal stands disposed of with no order as to costs.
ii) The record and proceedings be sent back to the learned Tribunal.
(NEERAJ P. DHOTE, J.) Tambaskar.
